messages:
mike: noticing intermittent DNS resolution failures from staging eu-west-1 GPU nodes after the NAT gateway change at ~22:10 UTC. External hostnames sometimes hang for 2-5s then fail. Pods in the dedicated pool affected.

anya: confirmed on a canary job — replies NXDOMAIN or SERVFAIL. hostNetwork: true pods OK, hostNetwork: false affected. Could be egress/NAT related.

infra-bot: NAT gateway update completed 2025-03-12T22:10Z by opsbot (change-4321).

julia: can you paste /etc/resolv.conf from an affected pod + a dig to a failing hostname?

mike: ```/etc/resolv.conf
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local
nameserver 10.0.0.2
options ndots:5 timeout:2 attempts:2 single-request-reopen edns0
```

mike: dig output to api.partner.example.com (from pod):
```; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> api.partner.example.com @10.0.0.2
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 45212
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 0, ADDITIONAL: 0
```

sam: same query from node host (not in pod) succeeds. So query path differs. Curl from pod to partner api times out, from host it works.

anya: hypothesis: upstream DNS provider is rate-limiting our new SNAT IPs after the NAT rotation. hostNetwork pods use node IPs (not the NAT'd EIP), so they avoid the throttle. Also suspect stub resolver behavior — we hit the single-request implementation and some upstreams drop UDP fragments.

sre-oncall: checked NAT GW logs: after rotation we started using a new EIP pool. Upstream partner logged REFUSED/THROTTLE for our new IPs (they flagged unusual query rate). Opening support ticket with them now.

julia: quick debug: can you run `curl -sS --dns-servers 8.8.8.8 http://api.partner.example.com/health` from a pod as a temp workaround? If that fixes app traffic we can add a fallback config.

mike: `curl` to 8.8.8.8 works from pod, resolves fast. So adding public fallback helps. Not ideal for private partner domains.

anya: other mitigation: add stubDomains entry in CoreDNS to forward partner domain to trusted resolver (hosted by partner), or pin kube-proxy/iptables to avoid NAT for DNS traffic. But we need ops coordination to change NAT EIP set or ask partner to whitelist new EIPs.

sam: I spun up a minimal pod with dnsPolicy: Default and hostNetwork: true -> resolves fine. Recreated broken pod without dnsmasq sidecar and it still failed, so it's not sidecar caching. TTL doesn't seem to be the issue.

julia: let's also check `resolv.conf` ndots/options — single-request-reopen sometimes helps with EDNS/IPv6 issues, but here the pattern points to upstream filtering.

sre-oncall: action plan proposed: 1) rollback NAT EIP rotation to previous stable EIP set (ops) 2) open ticket with partner to whitelist new EIPs and explain burst pattern 3) add CoreDNS stubDomains entry for partner domain as short-term fallback 4) add alerting for DNS SERVFAIL rate per node 5) create a canary with explicit fallback to 8.8.8.8 for verification. I'll start rollback now (ETA 15m).

infra-bot: Incident ticket INF-789 created: "DNS failures after NAT EIP rotation - staging eu-west-1".

mike: after rollback: verified resolution restored on 3/3 canaries. Keeping monitoring for 2h before closing. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

anya: follow-ups: add runbook step to validate upstream whitelist whenever we rotate NAT EIPs; document CoreDNS stub fallback pattern for partner domains.

julia: I'll file a docs PR with the runbook and add Grafana dashboard panels for dns SERVFAIL rates per node.

sre-oncall: rollback completed. Observability shows errors drop to baseline. Will keep thread open until midnight UTC.

sam: logging note: captured tcpdump on nat path — lots of truncated UDP responses and RSTs from upstream. Saved pcap to /var/log/pcaps/dns-nat-rotation.pcap for partner support.

mike: tagging partner contact @partner-support in ticket and sharing pcap.

anya: thanks — nice triage.
